text: In nineteen thirty-two, Australia went to war... against birds.
About twenty thousand emus had invaded the wheat farms of Western Australia.
They ate the crops, and smashed straight through the fences.
So the farmers, many of them ex-soldiers, asked the army for help.
The army sent three men. Two machine guns. Ten thousand bullets.
On day one, the emus took one look at the guns... and scattered in every direction.
Two days later, about a thousand emus walked straight toward an ambush.
This was it. The big moment. And then... the gun jammed.
The soldiers tried shooting from a truck. The emus simply outran it.
Each flock even had a lookout, one tall bird keeping watch. Big brain move.
After less than a week, the army pulled out, and politicians joked that the emus deserved medals.
Round two went a bit better. But in the end: nearly ten thousand bullets... for fewer than a thousand birds.
The commander even said these birds could take bullets like tanks.
The farmers asked for the army three more times. The answer? No.
Today, hundreds of thousands of emus still roam Australia. Undefeated.
